about: Which hazards are priced as property catastrophe perils in the insurance engine (ml/scoring/insurance_pricing.price_perils): each insured peril is priced on its own (its own score, occurrence probability and damage ratio) and accumulates in its own (peril, region) zone. A hazard not listed as insured is shown as context but never priced as property damage. A peril is priced only where its score is a likelihood or intensity scale for buildings (core/hazard_relevance: a susceptibility class is not an occurrence probability). Declared reading (Tellumen): the list follows the perils a property catastrophe cover indemnifies and the Solvency II standard-formula natural-catastrophe perils (windstorm, earthquake, flood, hail, subsidence — Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Articles 120-125), plus wildfire, volcanic and surface-water flooding, which property covers commonly include.

subsidence.note: priced only under a model whose scale is a measured intensity (the observed EGMS rate); the susceptibility class is not

landslide.note: priced only under a likelihood scale; the LHASA susceptibility class is not

drought.reason: a meteorological drought index is not property damage; its damaging effect on buildings (clay shrinkage) is the subsidence peril

heat_chronic.reason: chronic heat is an operating and health risk, not an insured property catastrophe

heat_acute.reason: a live nowcast, never a standing score

pollution.reason: air quality is not property damage

cold_wave.reason: freeze damage is an attritional escape-of-water claim, not a catastrophe peril in the standard formula

coastal_erosion.reason: gradual shoreline retreat is excluded from property covers as a gradual cause

saline_intrusion.reason: aquifer salinity is not property damage
